data.title: Stryker (SYK) President Sold Shares. How Much Do They Still Hold?
data.description:
• Group President of Global Quality & Operations Viju Menon sold $2.0m of Stryker (NYSE:SYK) stock on November 25, 2026.
  • The $2.0m disposal reduced their holding by 34%.

One director dominates Stryker insider selling

Viju Menon cut exposure after a year in which their filings show only one open-market sale and one option or award exercise, so the latest move reads as a continuation rather than a change in approach for this Stryker executive.

The heavier activity came from Independent Director Ronda Stryker, whose February 2026 sale of $181.7m followed full-year results and was part of a run of disposals that in total trimmed their holding by 3%. In the three months after that trade, the company reported first quarter earnings and launched its SmartHospital Platform. By late spring the shares were 19% lower than on the day of the sale, with Ronda Stryker returning to sell again in May.

Across these filings, the shares now trade close to the average sale prices for most of the insiders. The sale by M. Fink came at a level that was 17% below where the shares change hands today, a rise they missed on the stock they sold. Taken together, the past year reads as steady selling, concentrated in one director but shared across several managers, which leans more toward caution than confidence in the way Stryker insiders handle their own holdings.

Mako execution and hospital spending have to carry Stryker

For Stryker to make these insider sales look early, the business needs its robotics push and hospital capital cycle to keep doing the heavy lifting that underpins the Narrative. On October 29, 2026, the third quarter update showed higher sales than the prior year and a different profit mix, with the share price now close to where insiders were selling.

  • Mako needs wider use, more installations and broader procedures that pull through implants and recurring service income.
  • Hospital capital budgets need to keep supporting orders for Mako systems, beds and Smart Care equipment.
  • Peripheral vascular needs to rebuild volumes as manufacturing issues clear and new thrombectomy products gain traction.

Heavy insider holdings reshape what these trades mean

Several insiders sold on the open market, and the register shows that together they still own 9.3% of Stryker, a stake worth $11.5b, which is high for a company this size. Every trade comes from people whose own wealth moves with the stock. Independent Director Ronda Stryker, who traded earlier this year, is also the sixth-largest holder with 3.7% of the company, so each sale adjusts a significant personal position. John Brown is the third-largest holder with 5.3% of the company, and beside stakes this size, insider sales over the year barely change who controls the shares.

Insiders and major holders together make these trades read as portfolio moves inside a tightly held stock rather than shifts in who owns it.
